blocks.text: This is a change. So thank you, Ramocho, for the insights of the many challenges that are being faced by our refugee and immigrant community. I am here to provide a small update on how the Office of Language Services supports our refugee and immigrant community, especially our neighbors who might be learning English in accessing city services and programs and services. Thank you for the opportunity to speak with you today and to share the progress and purpose the office of language services an initiative rooted in equity access and community connection this office was initiated in 2018 as a program of the office of neighborhood engagement under the major strategic plan and officially instituted as an office in 2023 under the department of neighborhood engagement to foster greater connection between city government and and the communities we serve. Thank you for this honor and opportunity to lead this office and to lead our city in being more equitable and inclusive for all. Since its official formal launch, the Office of Language Services has made meaningful strides to ensure language is never a barrier to civic engagement, safety, or access to vital services. Here are some of the work we've done. We implemented the Propio One platform, a robust on-demand phone and video interpretation platform, offering access to over 300 professional interpreters in more than 300 languages 24-7. We have trained staff across all departments to effectively use the communication tools, empowering every city team member to engage with residents in their preferred language with confidence and professionalism. A centralized service request procedure was also developed to streamline internal requests for language services, improving efficiency, tracking, and resource management, and I have to thank our communications team who has been so supportive in helping me implement technology and procedures. The office has launched a dedicated intranet page for staff. This centralized hub includes our mission and vision language service request links, Propio One Access, even a demo video is in there, step-by-step usage guides as well. We also maintain a team of professionally trained bilingual English and Spanish staff members who are available to provide immediate in-house translation and interpretation services. Those team members are myself and Abraham Milano, who has joined the neighborhood engagement team and is such a vital person in our team. Let me share some brief impact data from the year 2024. Propia received 777 calls throughout the year 2024, serving residents in 23 different languages. We've responded to 129 language access requests, and we've completed in-house Spanish translations, totally more than 10,000 words in flyers, social media communications, and program information. And we continue to see strong and increasing use across departments. All departments are utilizing our tools and services. And a more robust report to council will be provided later this year. Beyond service delivery, the Office of Language Services conducts ongoing research onto local demographics and language trends and community needs, builds relationships with cultural organizations and community partners, and actively collaborates with other municipal departments to ensure we're continuously improving the accessibility and quality of language services. This is not a one-day work. It continues to improve and grow over time. This work is not simply technical, it is relational. It's about showing our refugee and immigrant neighbors that they belong. Thank you, Ramusha. That their voices matter, and that their access to information and services is not conditional on language ability. On behalf of the Office of Language Services, I want to express a deep gratitude to the mayor and city council for your continued commitment to this mission. Together, we're making Lancaster a more inclusive, connected and equitable city for all. Thank you for the opportunity and have a pleasant evening.
